name: University Park
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in University Park, TX 2026
seo_description: Kids' Christmas in University Park, TX: SMU Celebration of Lights on Nov 30 with Storytime with Santa, live reindeer and the Dallas Hall tree lighting.
lede: Christmas in University Park centers on Southern Methodist University, where the Celebration of Lights has lit Dallas Hall since 1977, with Storytime with Santa, live reindeer and a tree lighting. The Park Cities also keep their own city tree lightings and Santa visits.
sections: A Park Cities town built around a university

University Park grew up beside Southern Methodist University, which opened in 1915. The town was incorporated in 1924 with about 1,200 people, and Snider Plaza opened in 1927 as an early shopping village, according to the Texas State Historical Association. Residents adopted commission government on April 6, 1926. University Park and Highland Park together make up the Park Cities, and the two towns share the Highland Park Independent School District, so families in both towns are Park Cities neighbors. Its Christmas traditions today reach from the SMU campus to the city's own park.
How the Celebration of Lights began

SMU's magazine blog says the university first held the Festival of Lights on December 4, 1977, and renamed it Celebration of Lights in 1978. SMU news and the Daily Campus report that the first lights cost $5,000 and students climbed ladders to decorate the six pillars of Dallas Hall. The SMU Student Foundation, which organizes the evening, counts the 2026 event as the 49th. It says free food, live reindeer and a welcome for all Dallas communities and people are part of the night, and the ceremony still includes a reading of the Christmas story.
Tree lightings and Santa in the Park Cities

The Park Cities each keep a tree lighting tradition. The Town of Highland Park says its Big Pecan Tree is the oldest community Christmas tree lighting tradition in Dallas County. The City of University Park lists its own holiday programs on a Special Events page, including a tree lighting at Centennial Park and Santa visits, and the city's Santa page has listed Santa Around Town evenings for families. This page tracks only events whose hosts print a price, so some Park Cities events are still being checked.

faq: What is SMU Celebration of Lights?

It is Southern Methodist University's holiday tradition on the Dallas Hall Lawn, run by the SMU Student Foundation. It includes food, holiday music, Storytime with Santa, live reindeer, hot cocoa, a tree lighting ceremony and a reading of the Christmas story by the SMU president.
When did Celebration of Lights start?

SMU's magazine blog says the first Festival of Lights was held on December 4, 1977, and that it was renamed Celebration of Lights in 1978. The SMU Student Foundation, the student group that organizes the evening, counts the 2026 event as the 49th, so it has run for nearly five decades.
Is the event open to the public?

The SMU Student Foundation says all Dallas communities and people are welcome, and SMU's registration page calls the 2026 event complimentary. Check SMU's event page for registration details and any updates before you go, since the host controls how guests sign up.
Where is the Big Pecan Tree?

The Landmark Pecan Tree is in Highland Park, at 4202 Armstrong Parkway, a different town from University Park. The Town of Highland Park says its tree lighting is the oldest community Christmas tree lighting tradition in Dallas County, and the town's Big Pecan Tree page tells that story.
Can you take the train to SMU?

Yes. DART's SMU/Mockingbird Station, 5465 E Mockingbird Lane, is served by the Red, Blue and Orange lines, and the SMU Express bus connects the station with campus. DART lists the SMU Express on its bus routes page, so check its schedule for the evening before you go.
